references.text: The Israelites set out from Rameses to Succoth, describing the same departure from Rameses mentioned in Numbers 33:3.
The first month is noted as the beginning of the months for Israel, corresponding to the time given in Numbers 33:3.
The Passover lamb was to be slaughtered on the fourteenth day of the first month, the day before the departure on the fifteenth day.
The Lord brought the children of Israel out of Egypt, confirming the exodus mentioned in Numbers 33:3.
The children of Israel went out with a mighty hand, the same expression used in Numbers 33:3 regarding their triumphant departure.
Rameses is mentioned as one of the store cities the Israelites built in Egypt, the starting point of their journey.
Joseph settled his father and his brothers in the region of Rameses, which later became the starting point for the exodus.
